records.reported_metrics_raw: Euclidean-distance error for pressure and total velocity; surface pressure-coefficient agreement; target-shape recovery; online computational time.
records.metric_details_raw: The LF-PINN corrects low-fidelity flowfields toward ground truth with a mean improvement of approximately 19% in pressure and approximately 5% in total velocity, based on Euclidean-distance comparisons. Surface pressure-coefficient distributions improve particularly near the suction peak. In inverse design, the model approaches the expected target shapes while reducing online computational time by at least one order of magnitude relative to direct airfoil-analysis tools.

records.metric_details_raw: The conference abstract evaluates the PINN by comparing predicted surrounding-flow velocity contours with direct numerical simulation training data. Training minimizes sparse supervised flow-data loss and governing-equation residuals, while cylinder displacement is incorporated into the residual formulation. Hydrodynamic forces are evaluated from the PINN-predicted flow field through a force-partitioning method. The indexed abstract does not expose scalar errors.

records.metric_details_raw: The publication evaluates whether countercurrent spontaneous-imbibition observations identify the capillary diffusion coefficient and the underlying saturation functions. A complete recovery curve yields a unique correct diffusion coefficient and saturation profiles, while relative-permeability and capillary-pressure decompositions can remain nonunique. Limited early-time recovery admits multiple fitted diffusion coefficients and divergent future predictions; adding an in-situ saturation profile improves constraint, pressure data help constrain capillary pressure, and artificial noise broadens the range of estimated diffusion coefficients. Publicly indexed summaries do not expose scalar error values.
